1.17(i) Information related to procurements, tenders, bids, work contracts, rates etc. All goods and services are now being procured through GeM. For services not available on GeM, tenders are floated on Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal and details are also uploaded on the website under: Tenders.
1.17(ii) Public Private Partnership(PPP) Cabinet Secretariat does not deal with PPP Projects.
1.17(iii) Transfer policy and transfer orders Transfer policy or transfer orders of the officers fall within the domain of the respective cadre controlling authorities like DoPT.
1.17(iv) RTI Applications/ First Appeals and their replies Responses to the Frequently Asked Questions under RTI is Given on the website: RTI FAQs

Details of RTI applications / appeals disposed is also available on the website: Quarterly RTI Reports
1.17(v) Programmes to advance understanding of RTI Cabinet Secretariat sends its officers and staff for training programmes on RTI organized by training institutes such as Institute of Secretariat Training & Management (ISTM) from time to time. All guidelines/instructions on RTI issued by the Government of India are circulated to all officers/staff to enable them to participate in the training. Officers/ officials can also undertake RTI trainings through online platforms like iGot Karmayogi.
1.17(vi) Are the details of policies/ decisions which affect public, informed to them. The policies are formulated and implemented by the respective Ministries and Departments, consultation with members of public in regard to formulation of implementation of policy is undertaken by the respective Ministry/ Department.
The decisions of Cabinet and CCEA are accessible through a link More => Press Releases on the Website.
1.17(vii) Dissemination of information widely and in such form and manner which is easily accessible to public
[Section 4(3)]		 The Website of Cabinet Secretariat has all relevant information available in bilingual form which includes the Allocation of Business Rules/Transaction of Business Rules, Handbook/Instructions for preparation of Cabinet Notes and Note for the Committee of Secretaries. In addition, the Website also contains details of the Council of Ministries, the work allocation of officers, organizational chart showing the channel of submission, contact address of the organization, telephone directory and List of CPIOs/Appellate Authorities. Guidelines for foreign travel by Ministers of the Union Government and Chief Ministers/Ministers in States/UTs have been placed in the Website under the heading Circulars. The decisions of Cabinet and CCEA are accessible through a link More => Press Releases in the Website.
The Website also provides link to the other attached offices of Cabinet Secretariat i.e. Directorate of Public Grievances (DPG), Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Mission and National Authority for Chemical Weapons Convention (NACWC) and office of Principal Scientific Adviser.
The Website is Content Management Framework (CMF) compliant. The presentation of the Website is as per standardized framework for Government Websites and is user friendly.
1.17(viii) Accessibility of information. Available on the Website under Categories of Documents
1.17(ix) Information available in electronic form All relevant information pertaining to the work of Cabinet Secretariat is available in the Website. The Website is regularly updated. Decisions of the Cabinet and CCEA are accessible through a link More => Press Release

https://cabsec.gov.in/
1.17(x) Grievance redressal mechanism The Directorate of Public Grievances was set up in the Cabinet Secretariat in March,1989. Grievances can be filed either online or through post/drop-box with the Directorate of Public Grievance in respect of select Ministries/ Departments/ Organizations which have extensive public interface such as MTNL/BSNL, Railways, Posts, Insurance Companies, Public Sector Banks etc. (list is available at https://dpg.gov.in/Authpages/OgCovered.aspx)

Depending on nature and gravity of the grievances, the Directorate either seeks comments or transfers the same for appropriate action to the concerned Department(s).

Dr. T. V. Somanathan

CABINET SECRETARY

Dr. T. V. Somanathan is a distinguished Indian Administrative Service officer of the 1987 batch, Tamil Nadu cadre, currently serving as the Cabinet Secretary of India since 30 August 2024. With an illustrious career spanning over three decades, he has held several key positions at both national and international levels.

Prior to his appointment as Cabinet Secretary, Dr. Somanathan served as the Finance Secretary of India, heading the Department of Expenditure. His earlier roles at the Centre include serving as Additional Secretary and Joint Secretary in the Prime Minister Office (PMO), where he played a pivotal role in various governance and policy initiatives.

Internationally, Dr. Somanathan served as Director, Corporate Affairs at the World Bank Group in Washington, D.C., having initially joined through its prestigious Young Professionals Program. His expertise in public finance and economic policy has been widely recognized both in India and abroad.

In the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, he contributed significantly as Joint Secretary, focusing on reforms and regulatory frameworks that enhanced corporate governance.

Educational Qualifications

  • Ph.D. in Economics, University of Calcutta
  • Executive Development Program, Harvard Business School
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)
  • Cost Accountant (CMA)
  • Company Secretary (CS)

Dr. Somanathan combines deep academic insight with practical administrative experience, making him one of India most respected civil servants. His professional journey reflects a commitment to excellence, integrity, and nation-building.

My Visit is an initiative by Cabinet Secretary to facilitate Secretaries to Government of India and officers of State Governments to have a smooth and simple process of making an appointment.

Meeting the Cabinet Secretary.

As is the existing practice, officers and others wishing to meet the Cabinet Secretary may seek appointments by sending an e-mail to cabinetsy(at)nic(dot)in or telephoning to 011-23016696/23011241.

In addition to the above method, as a convenience to Secretaries (who may need to meet on urgent official business) and to officers of State Governments (whose visits to Delhi may be infrequent), an "Open House" system (a specified period during which officers may come without appointment) is also being introduced on a trial basis, until further notice.

The Open House timings are as follows:

S. No. Class of officers Timing of Open House
1. Secretaries to Govt. of India and equivalent officers 10:00 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. on Tuesdays, Thursdays & Fridays (except holidays)
2. Visiting All India Service officers from State Governments (i.e. who are based outside Delhi)

This will be on a first-come-first-served basis and limited to the specified time. Hence, if there are many visitors, some may not be able to meet. It is not intended for any long discussion. The Open House is also subject to cancellation without notice, if exigencies arise on a given day.

Due to security restrictions in Seva Teerth, those officers who wish to come during the Open House period and do not have the requisite passes, should communicate their name and vehicle number, in advance, to the Cabinet Secretary's office on telephone (Nos.011-23016696/23011241) so that messages can be sent to the Control Room for permitting their vehicle's entry in Seva Teerth.

Directorate of Public Grievances
The Directorate of Public Grievances was set up in the Cabinet Secretariat in March, 1988. Grievances can be filed either online or through post/drop-box with the Directorate of Public Grievance in respect of select Ministries/Departments/Organizations which have extensive public interface.
National Authority Chemical Weapons Convention (NACWC)
The National Authority Chemical Weapons Convention was constituted by the Cabinet Secretariat on 5th May, 1997. The Chemical Weapons Convention Act, 2000 (the Act), was enacted and came into force on 1st July, 2005. The Authority was established and notified under the CWC Act, 2000 on 13th June 2005.
Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (O/o PSA)
The Government of India established the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) in November 1999. The PSA's office aims to provide pragmatic and objective advice to the Prime Minister and the cabinet in matters of Science and Technology.
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)
DBT is a major reform initiative where benefits, cash or in kind, are delivered directly to targeted beneficiaries using Aadhaar. It envisages efficiency and inclusion in the delivery processes leading to greater accountability and transparency in the system.
